text:
maya: Heads up — nightly CI shows a ~20-30% p95 bump for small-batch (1-4) text gen after yesterday's infra merge that upgraded the CUDA compatibility packages. This looks like a release/blocker for the rollout. @eric @sam :eyes:

eric: saw the CI alert. linking the job: https://ci.internal/reds/nightly/7421 — failure only on smallbatch smoke, largebatch and embeddings are fine.

sam: quick note — the merge was the vendor/cuda-compat bump that pulled in libnvrtc 12.3.1->12.4.0 and a patched triton wheel (triton==2.7.3 -> 2.7.4). Could be ABI-level kernel selection differences.

ci-bot: nightly-run #7421: FAILURE — smallbatch p95 latency > threshold (baseline 42ms -> 60ms). Attached perf trace: s3://perf-traces/nightly/7421/smallbatch-nsys.qdrep

maya: started a short profiling run on a repro host (a100). Captured nsys + cuda-memcheck. Topline: extra memcpy(s) before kv prefetch path, and a new code path in triton/autotune that forces a non-kernelized prefetch for tiny sequences.

sam: can you paste the diff? I suspect the triton patch toggled a selector flag.

maya: here's the selector diff that landed (excerpt):

```diff
- selector: heuristic: prefer_gpu_prefetch: true
+ selector: heuristic: prefer_gpu_prefetch: auto
```

maya: with auto, the runtime is now probing a host-prefetch fallback on our A100 image which adds a synchronous memcpy per request for tiny sequences. That lines up with the increased tail.

eric: running git-bisect locally now across the vendor merge range. If bisect points to the triton wheel, we should pin back to 2.7.3 for the rollout.

sam: suggested quick mitigation: force selector to prefer_gpu_prefetch: true via env override to avoid host fallback. You can set REDWOOD_AUTOTUNE_PREFETCH=force_gpu in the runtime config.

maya: applied the env override on staging: REDWOOD_AUTOTUNE_PREFETCH=force_gpu. Re-ran the smallbatch suite. p95 dropped from 60ms -> 45ms ( ~25% improvement). Good signal.

eric: bisect result: commit 9f3b42c (vendor/cuda-compat bump) is the first bad commit; digging shows it pulled triton==2.7.4 which added the auto prefetchtoggle.

sam: plan: 1) pin triton to 2.7.3 in the release branch, 2) add CI smoke for smallbatch p95 on our GPU images, 3) follow up with a proper fix in autotune that doesn't synchronous-fallback for tiny sequences.

deployer: rolling a rollback build to canary with pinned triton 2.7.3 now. Canary will be up in ~10m.

perf-bot: canary-run #7421-canary: p95 smallbatch = 44ms (baseline 42ms) — within tolerance. :white_check_mark:

maya: ok let's hold the rollout. I'll open an internal issue with profiling artifacts and the nsys capture (s3 link). Also adding a regression test to catch host-prefetch fallbacks on small sequences.

eric: opened issue RED-5123 with stack traces and bisect notes. Assigning to @sam for autotune follow-up.

sam: thanks — I'll take it. Also proposing we add a short release note: "Pinned triton to 2.7.3 pending autotune fallback fix" so CS knows why a vendor bump was reverted.

maya: tagging the release manager and ops: @deployer please hold production rollout until RED-5123 resolved or we've validated the new triton with autotune fix.

deployer: holding rollout. Will update the release ticket. :hammer:
